description: Traffic per Proxmox guest, read from the hypervisor's side of each guest NIC (tapVMIDiN for VMs, vethVMIDiN for containers) and named by roles/pve_guest_metrics. It covers guests that run no collector, such as a firewall or Windows, and traffic between guests on one bridge, which no firewall sees. Direction is from the guest's point of view throughout.

panels.description: Everything arriving at the hypervisor's physical NICs, from the internet and the rest of the LAN alike. The Network dashboard's exclusion list plus tunnels (tailscale0, wg, tun): tunnel traffic already crosses a physical NIC encrypted, and counting both would count it twice.
panels.title: Hypervisor NICs In

panels.description: Everything leaving the hypervisor's physical NICs.
panels.title: Hypervisor NICs Out

panels.description: Sent plus received, right now. A router guest usually wins: it counts every forwarded byte twice, once on the way in and once on the way out.

targets.expr: topk(1, sum by (guest) (rate(node_network_receive_bytes_total{host=~"$host",device=~"(tap|veth)[0-9]+i[0-9]+"}[5m]) * on (host, device) group_left (guest) fleet_pve_guest_nic_info{host=~"$host",guest=~"$guest",bridge=~"$bridge"}) + sum by (guest) (rate(node_network_transmit_bytes_total{host=~"$host",device=~"(tap|veth)[0-9]+i[0-9]+"}[5m]) * on (host, device) group_left (guest) fleet_pve_guest_nic_info{host=~"$host",guest=~"$guest",bridge=~"$bridge"}))

panels.title: Busiest Guest Now

panels.description: Age of the guest-name file roles/pve_guest_metrics writes on the hypervisor every 5 minutes. Past 10 minutes the names on this page may be out of date, and a guest created since then is missing from it. No data means the role is not deployed on this host, and every panel below will be empty.
panels.title: Guest Names Refreshed

panels.description: The hypervisor's physical NICs, in above the line and out below it. This is the machine's whole conversation with the outside, internet and LAN together: the uplink port behind the main bridge carries almost all of it.
panels.title: Physical NICs

panels.description: What each guest NIC sends. Read from the hypervisor's side of the guest's virtual cable, so this is the host's RECEIVE counter on tapVMIDiN or vethVMIDiN: what the host receives is what the guest sent.

targets.expr: sum by (host, guest, nic) (rate(node_network_receive_bytes_total{host=~"$host",device=~"(tap|veth)[0-9]+i[0-9]+"}[5m]) * on (host, device) group_left (guest, nic) fleet_pve_guest_nic_info{host=~"$host",guest=~"$guest",bridge=~"$bridge"})

panels.title: Sent by Guest

panels.description: What each guest NIC receives: the host's TRANSMIT counter on the guest's device.

targets.expr: sum by (host, guest, nic) (rate(node_network_transmit_bytes_total{host=~"$host",device=~"(tap|veth)[0-9]+i[0-9]+"}[5m]) * on (host, device) group_left (guest, nic) fleet_pve_guest_nic_info{host=~"$host",guest=~"$guest",bridge=~"$bridge"})

panels.title: Received by Guest

panels.description: Bytes the guests put onto each bridge. On a bridge with no physical port and no host address, such as a firewall's LAN side, every frame comes from a guest, so this is everything that segment carries, including guest-to-guest traffic no firewall sees. On a bridge with an uplink, traffic from outside and from the hypervisor itself is not counted here.
panels.title: Sent per Bridge

panels.description: Packets the hypervisor dropped on a guest's device, either direction. Sustained drops usually mean the guest is not draining its queue fast enough: it is CPU-starved, or its NIC queue is too small for its traffic.

targets.expr: sum by (host, guest, nic) ((rate(node_network_receive_drop_total{host=~"$host",device=~"(tap|veth)[0-9]+i[0-9]+"}[5m]) + rate(node_network_transmit_drop_total{host=~"$host",device=~"(tap|veth)[0-9]+i[0-9]+"}[5m])) * on (host, device) group_left (guest, nic) fleet_pve_guest_nic_info{host=~"$host",guest=~"$guest",bridge=~"$bridge"})

panels.title: Dropped Packets per Guest NIC

panels.description: Total sent per guest NIC over the dashboard's time range. Capped by Prometheus retention, which is 7 days on the central stack.

targets.expr: sort_desc(sum by (guest, nic) (increase(node_network_receive_bytes_total{host=~"$host",device=~"(tap|veth)[0-9]+i[0-9]+"}[$__range]) * on (host, device) group_left (guest, nic) fleet_pve_guest_nic_info{host=~"$host",guest=~"$guest",bridge=~"$bridge"}))

panels.title: Most Data Sent, Selected Range

panels.description: Total received per guest NIC over the dashboard's time range.

targets.expr: sort_desc(sum by (guest, nic) (increase(node_network_transmit_bytes_total{host=~"$host",device=~"(tap|veth)[0-9]+i[0-9]+"}[$__range]) * on (host, device) group_left (guest, nic) fleet_pve_guest_nic_info{host=~"$host",guest=~"$guest",bridge=~"$bridge"}))

panels.title: Most Data Received, Selected Range

panels.description: One row per guest NIC. Seven days is the longest total available: the central Prometheus keeps 7 days, so a monthly figure needs longer retention first. A guest that restarted mid-window is still counted correctly; increase() handles the counter reset.

targets.expr: sum by (guest, vmid, nic, bridge) (increase(node_network_receive_bytes_total{host=~"$host",device=~"(tap|veth)[0-9]+i[0-9]+"}[24h]) * on (host, device) group_left (guest, vmid, nic, bridge) fleet_pve_guest_nic_info{host=~"$host",guest=~"$guest",bridge=~"$bridge"})

sum by (guest, vmid, nic, bridge) (increase(node_network_transmit_bytes_total{host=~"$host",device=~"(tap|veth)[0-9]+i[0-9]+"}[24h]) * on (host, device) group_left (guest, vmid, nic, bridge) fleet_pve_guest_nic_info{host=~"$host",guest=~"$guest",bridge=~"$bridge"})

sum by (guest, vmid, nic, bridge) (increase(node_network_receive_bytes_total{host=~"$host",device=~"(tap|veth)[0-9]+i[0-9]+"}[7d]) * on (host, device) group_left (guest, vmid, nic, bridge) fleet_pve_guest_nic_info{host=~"$host",guest=~"$guest",bridge=~"$bridge"})

sum by (guest, vmid, nic, bridge) (increase(node_network_transmit_bytes_total{host=~"$host",device=~"(tap|veth)[0-9]+i[0-9]+"}[7d]) * on (host, device) group_left (guest, vmid, nic, bridge) fleet_pve_guest_nic_info{host=~"$host",guest=~"$guest",bridge=~"$bridge"})

panels.title: Per Guest NIC Totals
